newsitem.title: UK: Dollar fails to shake narrow ranges by late Europe.
newsitem.headline: Dollar fails to shake narrow ranges by late Europe.

text.p: The dollar stuck steadfastly within the European session's narrow ranges by late trade, managing to claw a few ticks higher against the mark but remaining mostly stable against the yen.
A stronger-than-expected U.S. consumer confidence report for August had little impact on the dollar while U.S. debt futures recovered from an initial dip on the data.

"The figures suggest that we could get a strong employment report next week," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International. "It shows investors should be wary of U.S. assets, so dollar upside could be limited."
Although the report showed rising consumer confidence, Stamenkovic was cautious over the data's mixed signals for jobs which saw a rise in families saying jobs were "hard to get".
The confidence index was at 109.4 against analysts' forecasts of around 105.0 and July's revised figure of 107.0.
Dealers said that forex activity remained light with little news in the short-term to shake the dollar out of its current ranges apart from Wednesday's Tankan quarterly survey in Japan.
"Besides the Tankan, there's nothing really until the U.S. jobs numbers next week," said a UK bank corporate dealer. "There is still the summer malaise hanging over the market."
By 1528 GMT, the dollar was little changed from Monday levels, trading at 1.4778/81 marks and 107.75/80 yen against 1.4771/75 and 107.70/75 late Monday.
Although few see the Bank of Japan altering its steady monetary policy stance after Tankan release, market nervousness ahead of the survey was keeping the short-term bias towards a firmer yen.

The mark remained steady on the crosses in choppy afternoon trade, underpinned by renewed concerns over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) and the forthcoming round of European 1997 budget negotiations.
Comments by senior Italian and German officials over recent days has rekindled the debate of a delay in the EMU timetable or a dilution of its criteria.
Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said late Monday that a softening of EMU criteria was "out of the question".
The Swiss franc was slightly easier against the mark and dollar in late European trade, trading at 80.72/74 centimes per mark and 1.1935/39 francs per dollar at 1600 GMT.
It stood at 80.66 centimes and 1.1905/15 late Monday.
